record.paper_title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Do multisoliton states exist for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on star graphs, and what happens when several solitons collide simultaneously at a vertex? In particular, can one construct or analyze solutions representing more than one incoming or outgoing soliton interacting through the junction?

evidence.quote: Nothing it is presently known about the possible existence of multisolitons, or about the collision of several solitons at the vertex.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation on a star graph G consisting of N≥2 half-lines (edges) e_1,...,e_N joined at a common vertex v. On each edge e_j, parametrize points by x∈[0,∞) with x=0 corresponding to v, and let ψ_j(t,x) denote the wavefunction component on edge e_j. The dynamics on each edge is governed by

  i ∂_t ψ_j = -∂_x^2 ψ_j - |ψ_j|^{2σ} ψ_j,  x>0, j=1,...,N,

with σ>0 (e.g. the cubic case σ=1), supplemented at the vertex by a self-adjoint coupling such as the Kirchhoff condition
  ψ_1(t,0) = ψ_2(t,0) = ... = ψ_N(t,0),  Σ_{j=1}^N ∂_x ψ_j(t,0+) = 0,
or a δ-type condition Σ_j ∂_x ψ_j(t,0+) = α ψ(t,0) with α∈ℝ.

A "soliton" on edge e_j is a localized traveling-wave profile of the form
  φ_{c,v_0}(t,x) = e^{i(v_0 x/2 - (v_0^2/4 - c)t)} R_c(x - v_0 t - x_0),
where R_c is the solitary-wave profile of the homogeneous line NLS (e.g. R_c(y) = (c(σ+1))^{1/(2σ)} sech^{1/σ}(σ√c · y) for the focusing power nonlinearity).

Question. Do there exist, for the NLS evolution above on the star graph, "multisoliton" solutions, i.e. solutions ψ(t)=(ψ_1(t),...,ψ_N(t)) which, as t→±∞, asymptotically decompose into a finite collection of solitons of the above form moving along the edges, with at least two solitons either incoming toward or outgoing from the vertex? Furthermore, analyze the simultaneous collision of several solitons at the vertex: construct or rigorously describe the scattering map relating the incoming asymptotic soliton data to the outgoing asymptotic soliton data when two or more solitons reach the junction v at the same time.
artifact.status_search_result: Search results show some progress on related questions: integrable matrix NLS on star graphs admits multisoliton solutions via Hirota's method under special integrability assumptions, and fast-soliton scattering through a Y-junction has been analyzed in the cubic case. However, no general rigorous construction or classification of multisoliton solutions on star graphs with standard (e.g. Kirchhoff or δ) vertex conditions, including simultaneous multi-soliton collisions at the vertex, has been clearly established in the search evidence. The status of the general problem appears unresolved, with only partial results in special regimes.

status_evidence.title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation on graphs: recent results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing standing waves of NLS on graphs and scattering of fast solitons through a Y-junction in the cubic case.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results (fast-soliton scattering on Y-junctions, standing waves) are reported; multisoliton existence and simultaneous vertex collisions are listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Lax Pair Formulation and Multi-soliton Solution of the Integrable Vector NLS
status_evidence.snippet: Multisoliton solutions on a star graph via Hirota's bilinearization for an integrable matrix NLS with bond-dependent nonlinearities.
status_evidence.claim: Multisoliton solutions exist in special integrable settings on star graphs, indicating partial progress rather than a resolution of the general problem.

status_evidence.title: On the orbital instability of excited states for the NLS equation with the δ-interaction on a star graph
status_evidence.snippet: Studies stationary/excited states for NLS with δ-interaction on a star graph; does not address dynamical multisoliton collisions at the vertex.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work focuses on stationary states and stability rather than dynamic multisoliton collisions, leaving the multisoliton collision question unresolved.
